description: List every model one exact part number is documented to fit. Use check_part_fits instead for yes/no against specific named models, or to compare several part numbers at once. Use get_part instead for the full part record. Use get_model_parts instead for the reverse (model → parts). Use search_parts instead for keyword text. Part numbers match as in get_part (case, dashes, spaces, leading zeros, retired numbers); several matches return status ambiguous — ask which number is printed on the part. Not found is an error result; a part with no documented models returns fits [] and fit_status no_documented_fit. Neither means incompatible. Screen fits may include panel_options.

client.description: Optional: your agent or app name (letters and digits), used only for anonymous usage counts.

part_number.description: Required. OEM part number, with or without dashes or spaces, e.g. "01FR025", "7K4PW", "L78555-005".

name: get_part_fits

display_name.description: Short human label; not an identifier

fit_status.description: no_documented_fit: there is no fit or no result: LPF has no OEM document for it. Never means incompatible. not_asserted: a did-you-mean suggestion; no fit claim is made.

outcome.description: Always present. One field to branch on for every tool: found | no_documented_fit (identified, but no OEM-documented fit; never means incompatible) | needs_clarification (ask the user; see clarifying_question/candidates) | not_found (nothing LPF covers matches). Full contract: /api/states

title: Get models a part fits
